A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CacheFlow and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renaming, relocation and the change of publication format.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction, density-estimation, runtime and ablation results on Human3.6M and AMASS, including results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds zero-shot 3DPW evaluation, computational and memory measurements, and additional GMM-only and realism comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 revises the stated flow-training source from conditional q_phi(z|c) to standard-Gaussian q(z), a localized change in the method specification. The joint objective, cached triplets and nearest-neighbor inference remain unchanged. Explicit descriptions of frozen encoders/decoders and RNN outputs add documentation rather than establish further architectural changes.

E1.justification: v2 retains Human3.6M and AMASS and adds evaluation on in-the-wild 3DPW using AMASS-trained models and an AMASS-only cache (Section 5.3.1, Table 3). This substantially extends coverage to an explicit unseen-domain scenario relevant to the cache's generalization.

E2.justification: SkeletonDiff. (Curreli et al., 2025) is added to the existing Human3.6M/AMASS comparison in Table 1. The earlier comparator rows and Table 2 density-estimation comparators remain. FlowPrecomp. and its no-precomputation variant are renamed CacheFlow and w/o Cache; the GMM-only comparison revisits an already tested no-flow alternative.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an AMASS-to-3DPW protocol without fine-tuning, CPU/TITAN RTX resource measurements, and FID evaluation. Original benchmark splits, prediction horizons and sampling protocols remain. Appendix A reports batch size 192 for Human3.6M, versus v1's 64, but v2's main text still states 64; this reporting conflict does not establish which setting was used or whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds domain-shift robustness testing, computational and memory cost analysis, and an APD-versus-realism analysis using FID and reported failure cases. Table 6 further examines the GMM-only alternative with additional metrics. The original five-component ablation is retained as Section 5.3.3/Table 5, moved from v1 Appendix B/Table 3.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix A newly states that random seeds were fixed to 0 across all experiments; v1 provides no seed information. This disclosure does not establish additional runs. Neither version reports across-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests for performance.

E6.justification: Matched scores in Tables 1–2 and the original ablation remain unchanged. Added results include CacheFlow's 3DPW ADE/FDE of 0.499/0.591, cache sizes of 24.07/46.90 MB, platform-specific timings, GMM-only scores and FID of 0.196. SkeletonDiff.'s Human3.6M ADE of 0.344 changes the best reported ADE from SLD's 0.348. These are added results, not same-setting CacheFlow improvements.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13 retain the change-of-variables derivation, flow-matching relations, joint loss and sampling rule. No theorem or proof is added or revised. The new memory-size formula provides elementary resource accounting rather than substantive theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same core contributions: cached unconditional flows enable millisecond inference, explicit density estimation and competitive prediction accuracy. The approximately 4× and 30× speed claims also remain unchanged; the added experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of generalization beyond memorization, the tradeoff between APD and realism, cache adaptation without retraining, and demographic bias risks. Section 5.3.1's novel-future explanation is not reconciled with the retained conclusion's restriction to precomputed motions. Appendix F also asserts adaptation and continual learning without forgetting without corresponding experimental validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds frozen encoder/decoder and RNN parameterization details, PyTorch and Adam settings, CPU hardware, cache populations, storage requirements and precomputation costs. Its abstract supplies a code/model repository instead of only promising release. These substantially expand practical documentation, although Appendix A claims to specify training epochs without giving a count and contains the batch-size conflict noted under E3.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 positions CacheFlow against MDM, MotionGPT and MotionLM through their inference costs. References also add SkeletonDiff., Rectified Flow, SMPL and 3DPW. This is a bounded expansion and correction of the surrounding literature; the original FlowChain comparison and central efficiency positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section order remain intact. v2 makes local language corrections and explanatory additions, updates author/header information and citation style, moves the ablation discussion into Section 5.3.3, and reorganizes the appendices around added material. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the TMLR layout, changes headers, typography, table-caption placement and result highlighting, and adds Tables 3, 4, 6 and 7. Table 1 gains a comparator row, while the old ablation table moves into the main text as Table 5. All four figures retain their artwork; Figure 4's caption gains clarification.

improvement.justification: v2's zero-shot evaluation and cache construction, storage and hardware measurements address practical questions left unmeasured in v1 (Tables 3–4); FID adds useful realism evidence. These gains are tempered by conflicting batch settings, unexplained differences between the new GMM-only scores and retained no-flow ablation, and insufficiently supported adaptation claims. The additional evidence yields a limited net improvement while important clarity and reproducibility gaps remain.
